nameStory: The Marvel of Peru gets its name from early European explorers who were amazed by this 'wonderful' plant from the New World - 'Mirabilis' literally means 'wonderful' in Latin. It's also called Four O'Clock because its flowers have a magical daily routine, opening reliably in late afternoon around 4 PM and staying open through the night. Despite the name 'Peru,' this marvel actually comes from tropical America, including Mexico.
description: Marvel of Peru is a bushy annual flower that grows 2-4 feet tall and wide, creating a rounded, dense plant. It produces trumpet-shaped flowers that come in vibrant colors including pink, yellow, red, white, and even striped combinations - sometimes multiple colors appear on the same plant! The flowers have a unique daily schedule, opening in late afternoon and closing by morning. This old-fashioned garden favorite has oval, bright green leaves and thick, somewhat succulent stems.

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Trumpet-shaped flowers about 1 inch across that open only in late afternoon and evening, releasing an intense sweet fragrance that you can smell from several feet away. Colors range from white to pink, red, yellow, or striped combinations.

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Oval, smooth-edged leaves that are bright green and feel slightly thick and succulent to the touch, arranged opposite each other on the stems.

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Forms a bushy, rounded mound 2-4 feet tall and wide with multiple branching stems that feel thick and somewhat fleshy when you squeeze them gently.

idTips.label: Seeds
idTips.description: Produces large, wrinkled, black seeds about the size of peppercorns that are easy to collect and save - they feel hard and bumpy between your fingers.

habitat: In New England, Marvel of Peru is found exclusively in cultivated gardens, flower beds, and occasionally escaped near old homesites where it may self-seed. It thrives in full sun to partial shade in well-drained garden soil and is commonly grown as an annual ornamental. You won't find it growing wild in natural areas, but it may persist around abandoned gardens or spread from bird-scattered seeds.

seasonality.spring: Seeds are planted after last frost in late May. Young plants emerge as small green shoots with oval leaves.
seasonality.summer: Peak blooming season with flowers opening every late afternoon and closing by morning. Plants reach full size and continue producing new flowers daily.
seasonality.fall: Continues blooming until first hard frost kills the plant. Large black seeds mature and can be collected for next year's garden.
seasonality.winter: Plant dies completely with frost. Only the seeds survive, either collected by gardeners or naturally scattered.

funFact: Marvel of Peru is like a living clock - Indigenous peoples and early settlers could actually tell time by watching its flowers open punctually around 4-6 PM each day, earning it the nickname 'Four O'Clock.' Even more amazingly, the same plant can produce flowers of completely different colors and patterns, with some flowers being solid colored while others are striped or spotted!
confusionNotes: Marvel of Peru might be confused with morning glories, but remember the opposite timing trick - morning glories open in the morning and close during the day, while Four O'Clocks open in late afternoon. Morning glories also have heart-shaped leaves and climb on vines, while Marvel of Peru has oval leaves and grows as a bushy mound.
contextualKnowledge: Despite its name 'Marvel of Peru,' this plant actually originates from Mexico and tropical America, not Peru - early botanists often got geographic origins mixed up. It's been cultivated for over 500 years since the Aztecs grew it, and it became Connecticut's official children's state flower in memory of Michaela Petit, making it one of the few non-native plants to receive such an honor.
compareHints: Marvel of Peru is much more commonly grown than its wild relative, Wild Four O'Clock, which has smaller, less showy flowers and grows naturally in prairie regions. While both open their flowers in late afternoon, Marvel of Peru has much larger, more colorful blooms and grows as a garden ornamental, whereas Wild Four O'Clock has tiny pink flowers and grows in natural grasslands outside of New England.
